definition.label: Appeal to authority
definition.definition: Relying on a person or institution's status as if it settles the argument, especially when the relevant evidence, expertise, or consensus has not been shown.

source.currentDescription: Since naturalism excludes supernatural intervention rather than idealism, Kastrup concludes that analytic idealism can describe nature as spontaneously unfolding according to physical regularities.
source.lockedProposition: Naturalism excludes supernatural intervention and is compatible with nature unfolding spontaneously according to physical regularities.
source.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: characterizations there well to me naturalism and to most philosophers i know naturalism is the notion that what exists is natural so we are only excluding supernaturalism which basically doesn't exclude any serious person or position engaged in this debate so for me naturalism is it's the idea that nature unfolds spontaneously according to the patterns and regularities we call the laws of physics
source.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Kastrup clearly separates naturalism from physicalism, placing analytic idealism within a lawful, spontaneously unfolding nature and blocking the easy but inaccurate inference that his consciousness-first ontology invokes supernatural intervention. Principal limitation: His appeal to what naturalism means to most philosophers is informal, and the assertion that supernaturalism excludes no serious participant reaches beyond what the terminological clarification requires. Live burden: Kastrup must proceed from compatibility to superiority, showing not merely that idealism may count as naturalistic but that its ontology explains consciousness, external reality, and scientific findings more economically than Oppy’s pluralist naturalism.

presentedReviews.rationale: Mentioning what most known philosophers mean provides informal terminological support, but their status is not offered as settling idealism's compatibility with naturalism.
The reference to what most familiar philosophers mean is informal support for a terminological clarification, not reliance on their status as settling the substantive comparison.

definition.label: Equivocation
definition.definition: Shifting the meaning of a key word or phrase during the argument, making the reasoning seem stronger than it is.

source.currentDescription: Kastrup alleges tension between identifying experience with physical arrangements and denying a cat’s reduction to physical properties, asking Oppy to reconcile those commitments.
source.lockedProposition: Identifying experience with physical arrangements appears inconsistent with denying that a cat can be reduced to physical properties alone.

source.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Kastrup juxtaposes Oppy’s identification of experience with physical arrangements against his refusal to reduce cat-talk to physical vocabulary, posing a focused reconciliation challenge. Principal limitation: The inconsistency depends on equating explanatory irreducibility with nonphysical constitution, although Oppy’s cat claim concerns vocabulary’s descriptive insufficiency whereas his experience claim concerns theoretical identity. Live burden: Kastrup must identify a tension surviving that distinction, perhaps by showing that indispensable mental descriptions supply explanatory content incompatible with, or inaccessible to, the asserted neural identity.

presentedReviews.rationale: The alleged contradiction materially trades between reduction as physical constitution and reduction as exhaustive description in fundamental-physics vocabulary, exactly the conflation identified by the assessment.

definition.label: Begging the question
definition.definition: Assuming, directly or indirectly, the very point that needs to be established, so the conclusion is smuggled into the premises.

source.currentDescription: Because idealism also predicts mind-brain correlations as the appearance of experience, Kastrup concludes that correlation alone cannot discriminate identity theory from analytic idealism.
source.lockedProposition: Mind-brain correlations do not uniquely favor physicalism because idealism can also account for them as appearances of conscious experience.
source.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: to appeal to the correlates between patterns of brain activity and conscious experience it's an appeal to a correlate if i say that patterns of brain activity are just what conscious experience looks like i have accounted for those correlations so this is only an argument for physicalism so far as you actually beg the question of physicalism and you attribute the conclusion you want to extract
source.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Kastrup answers Oppy’s strongest empirical point at its decisive inference, granting neural correlation while supplying a concrete rival explanation under which brain activity is what conscious processes look like externally. Principal limitation: Demonstrating underdetermination by correlation does not independently validate the appearance relation, and describing Oppy’s inference as already assuming its conclusion slightly overstates what an abductive argument claims. Live burden: Kastrup must show that his account explains the detailed structure and intervention sensitivity of neural dependence at least as well, with fewer unsupported commitments than embedded identity.

presentedReviews.rationale: Kastrup explicitly accuses Oppy of assuming physicalism, but the assessment notes that this overstates an abductive inference; the move itself does not circularly assume its own conclusion.

source.currentDescription: A quantitative neural description excludes qualitative character by construction, Kastrup argues, so extracting experience from it mistakes a map of reality for the territory.
source.lockedProposition: Physicalism replaces reality with a quantitative description that excludes qualities by construction, so deriving qualities from it is like pulling territory from a map.

source.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Kastrup presents his most forceful explanatory challenge by distinguishing qualitative reality from quantitative description and illustrating the missing derivation through the memorable map-and-territory comparison. Principal limitation: The move treats Oppy’s broad pluralistic naturalism as though it were exhaustively quantitative physicalism, and a failure of derivation establishes an explanatory gap more readily than contradiction. Live burden: Kastrup must show that Oppy’s mental vocabulary cannot preserve qualities within a non-eliminative identity and that positing subjectivity as primitive explains, rather than simply assumes, their presence.

definition.label: Red herring
definition.definition: Diverting attention from the issue under dispute to a related but less relevant point, leaving the original challenge insufficiently answered.

definition.label: Ambiguity effect
definition.definition: Preferring clearer or more familiar claims over uncertain ones, even when the uncertain option may deserve serious consideration.

source.sectionTitle: Perception, theoretical entities, and external reality
source.currentDescription: Because quantum theory should recover the ordinary material world through decoherence, Oppy judges interpretations preserving that continuity more plausible than idealistic alternatives.
source.lockedProposition: A satisfactory quantum interpretation should recover the common-sense material world through decoherence, which Oppy finds more plausible than idealistic interpretations.
source.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: because there are some people who think that really there's a kind of requirement decoherence you better be able to get back um the the common sense world material world that we live in and that kind of approach to quantum mechanics strikes me as much more plausible than the kind of ideal unsurprisingly and idealistic interpretations of quantum mechanics
source.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Oppy identifies a legitimate adequacy constraint for quantum interpretation: a fundamental theory should recover the stable common-sense world in which experiments, apparatus, and observers operate. Principal limitation: He does not specify the favored interpretation or show that decoherence alone solves the measurement problem, and his comparative plausibility judgment receives almost no developed support against idealistic readings. Live burden: Oppy must explain how classicality emerges without presupposition, distinguish operational suppression of interference from a full interpretation, and show why recovering material appearances requires naturalist ontology rather than Kastrup’s objective experiential world.

presentedReviews.rationale: Oppy favors a commonsense-world constraint over an idealistic interpretation without developing the comparison, but the text does not establish a preference caused by uncertainty or familiarity.
Oppy favors recovery of the familiar material world, but the move does not establish a psychological preference for clarity over uncertainty; it offers an underdeveloped adequacy constraint instead.

source.currentDescription: Since decoherence presupposes a classical environment rather than explaining its emergence, Kastrup concludes that it is operationally useful but does not solve the measurement problem.
source.lockedProposition: Decoherence assumes an already classical environment, so it is a useful operational tool rather than an explanation of the measurement problem.
source.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: operational advantage of the coherence but of course it doesn't explain how the environment became classical in the first place which it needs to be if the coherence is to have any operational validity any explanatory power so in fact the coherence is not an interpretation it's not an account for the measurement problem at all it's a very useful operational tool
source.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Kastrup directly separates operational usefulness from interpretive explanation and identifies a specific circularity concern: decoherence cannot explain classicality if its practical application already assumes an effectively classical environment. Principal limitation: The quantum discussion is compressed, and the categorical statement that decoherence is no account at all risks overlooking interpretations in which it forms part of a broader solution. Live burden: Kastrup must show that Oppy’s preferred naturalistic family cannot supplement decoherence adequately and that the remaining measurement problem gives positive comparative support to analytic idealism rather than merely weakening one rival route.

source.sectionTitle: Perception, theoretical entities, and external reality
source.currentDescription: Oppy argues that metaphysical interpretation must preserve the material experimental standpoint supplying its evidence, lest it undermine the branch from which its conclusion was inferred.
source.lockedProposition: A metaphysical interpretation of material experiments should recover the material world and cannot coherently discard the evidential basis on which it relies.
source.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: i certainly wouldn't want to go down ravelli's route but i don't want to go down your route either it seems to me that you kind of where we start is where we have to end up with you know a material world experimentalist doing experiments with um material objects uh and you can't end up cutting off the branch that you were sitting on when you started so
source.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Oppy raises an important epistemic constraint: a metaphysical interpretation should preserve the reliability of experimenters, apparatus, and observed objects that supply the evidence from which it reasons. Principal limitation: Kastrup explicitly accepts an objective external world as appearance, so reinterpretation of material ontology does not necessarily discard experiments or sever their evidential basis; the objection risks assuming the conclusion it seeks. Live burden: Oppy must demonstrate an actual incompatibility between analytic idealism and trustworthy experimentation rather than treating ontological materiality as required for empirical objectivity.

presentedReviews.rationale: The branch-cutting objection treats ontologically material experimenters and objects as necessary for empirical evidence, thereby assuming the material ontology disputed by idealism, as the assessment recognizes.

presentedReviews.rationale: The branch-cutting objection presumes that reliable experiments require the material ontology under dispute, thereby importing the needed conclusion instead of showing idealism undermines evidence.

definition.label: Argument from ignorance
definition.definition: Treating a claim as true because it has not been disproved, or false because it has not been proved, rather than supplying positive evidence.

source.sectionTitle: Perception, theoretical entities, and external reality
source.currentDescription: Since experiments always require interpretation and unknown theories may remain, Oppy concludes that quantum evidence does not uniquely establish Kastrup’s relational-idealist metaphysics.
source.lockedProposition: Because experiments require interpretation and may omit something, Oppy finds it more plausible that something is missing than that Rovelli is right.
source.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: so it isn't just the experiments though because you have to interpret them and then you have to be confident that you're not missing something and when you think about okay saying what we're what we would be being asked to believe if we went with ravelli i think that it's much more plausible that we're missing something than that he's right
source.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Oppy correctly emphasizes empirical underdetermination, separating experimental results from their metaphysical interpretation and identifying the possibility that presently missing theory could alter the comparison. Principal limitation: Merely invoking an unspecified missing possibility blocks entailment but does not justify Oppy’s stronger judgment that such a possibility is more plausible than the relational interpretation under discussion. Live burden: Oppy must offer concrete rival explanations or symmetric standards for comparing interpretations, while Kastrup retains the burden of showing that experiments do more than narrow the field and positively favor analytic idealism.

presentedReviews.rationale: Invoking the possibility of missing theory weakens claimed entailment but does not itself treat a proposition as true merely because it has not been disproved.

Invoking the possibility of missing theory is speculative and inadequately supports the comparative plausibility judgment, but Oppy does not treat a proposition as true merely because it is unrefuted.

definition.label: Scope neglect
definition.definition: Failing to adjust judgment in proportion to the scale, number, or magnitude of what is being discussed.

source.sectionTitle: Mind-brain dependence, dissociation, and altered states
source.currentDescription: Clinical dissociation partitions an integrated mind into centers with distinct experiences, memories, and dispositions; Kastrup uses this as an empirical model for individual minds.
source.lockedProposition: Psychiatric dissociation is empirically established and involves one integrated mind seemingly partitioning into centers with distinct experiences, memories, and dispositions.
source.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: advent of neuroimaging so dissociation is an empirically established phenomenon in which what is originally one integrated mind seemingly partitions itself or breaks itself down into different centers of awareness different centers of phenomenal experience which contain different contents different memories different dispositions
source.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Kastrup supplies a recognizable empirical analogue for plurality within mentality, describing differentiated centers of awareness, memory, and disposition rather than invoking dissociation as an empty metaphor. Principal limitation: Evidence that one human mind can display partitioned functioning does not by itself show that a transpersonal field dissociates into organisms, and the scale-changing bridge remains unsupported. Live burden: Kastrup must identify structural similarities strong enough to justify extrapolation, explain the formation and maintenance of cosmic boundaries, and show why dissociation predicts the observed mind-brain relationship better than naturalistic alternatives.

presentedReviews.rationale: The unsupported extrapolation from clinical dissociation to cosmic individuation is a scale-bridge problem, but the text does not reveal judgment insensitive to magnitude as the bias definition requires.
The unsupported extrapolation from clinical dissociation to cosmic individuation changes scale, but the excerpt does not itself make a judgment that fails to adjust proportionally to magnitude.

definition.label: Base-rate neglect
definition.definition: Underweighting general background rates or prior probabilities while focusing too heavily on a vivid specific case or local detail.

source.sectionTitle: Mind-brain dependence, dissociation, and altered states
source.currentDescription: A reported dissociative-identity case connected a blind alter’s executive control with disappearing visual-cortex activity despite open eyes, supporting dissociation’s capacity to organize perception physiologically.
source.lockedProposition: In a dissociative-identity case, visual-cortex activity reportedly disappeared while a blind alter had executive control, although the subject's eyes remained open.
source.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: dissociative identity disorder was instrumented with an eeg cap and when one of the outers or the subsets of that mind technically called an altar when one of the altars that claimed to be blind uh had executive control uh the brain activity in the woman's visual cortex at the back of the head would just disappear although her eyes were open that's not
source.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Kastrup offers a concrete, testable case connecting dissociative state, reported blindness, open eyes, and altered visual-cortex activity, giving his mechanism more empirical substance than a purely conceptual analogy. Principal limitation: A single narrated EEG case arrives without methodological details, controls, representativeness, or consideration of alternative neurological explanations, and “disappear” may overstate the measurement. Live burden: Kastrup must establish what the study actually demonstrates, connect state-dependent neural changes to transpersonal dissociation, and show why the result favors body-as-appearance over ordinary mind-brain dependence.

presentedReviews.rationale: Reliance on one narrated case raises representativeness and alternative-explanation concerns, but no relevant background rate is supplied and then materially underweighted.
A single vivid case lacks representativeness and controls, but neither the reasoning nor assessment identifies a relevant background rate that Kastrup underweights.

definition.label: Special pleading
definition.definition: Applying an exception or different standard to one side of the argument without giving a principled reason for the difference.

source.currentDescription: Oppy concedes Kastrup’s evidential rule that belief should not outrun decent reasons, concluding that unsupported entities like the Flying Spaghetti Monster should not be believed in.
source.lockedProposition: Oppy agrees that ontological belief should not exceed what available reasons support.
source.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: to agree with the last bit of what you're saying there right you shouldn't you shouldn't believe in more than you've got decent reason to believe in and you just don't have decent reason to believe in the flying spaghetti monster so you shouldn't
source.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Oppy plainly accepts Kastrup’s evidential maxim, demonstrating methodological common ground and proportioning ontological belief to the reasons actually available rather than inflating disagreement. Principal limitation: The flying-spaghetti-monster illustration adds little analytical content, and the shared rule provides almost no comparative leverage unless either side shows which commitments lack decent support. Live burden: Oppy must apply the maxim to his own mind-brain identity and causal naturalism as rigorously as to universal subjectivity and dissociation, avoiding an asymmetric presumption in favor of familiar ontology.

presentedReviews.rationale: The assessment warns that the evidential maxim must be applied symmetrically, but this move merely accepts the maxim and does not yet apply a different standard to either ontology.
